decisions.rationale: Lead immediate special pressure with Mega Alakazam available to outrun and threaten Mega Gengar, while Floette-Eternal pressures Tyranitar and provides strong neutral damage. Garchomp covers the opposing Steel/sand core, and Talonflame supplies priority Tailwind plus disruption.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 registered four: Alakazam, Floette-Eternal, Garchomp, Talonflame. Preserve Mega Alakazam as the primary immediate Mega Gengar answer; Mega Floette remains an alternate endgame option if Gengar and Gholdengo are controlled. Garchomp is the main pressure into Tyranitar/Excadrill/Gholdengo, while Talonflame provides Tailwind and Taunt.

decisions.rationale: Lead the Sand core (Tyranitar + Excadrill): Sand Stream activates on entry giving Excadrill 280 effective Speed under Sand Rush, outspeeding the entire opponent roster. Excadrill's Focus Sash insurance + Iron Head (2x Floette), Rock Slide (4x Talonflame, spread), and High Horsepower (2x Garchomp) provide optimal coverage. Tyranitar adds Rock Slide spread and special bulk. Gengar-Mega in back provides Shadow Tag trapping to eliminate Floette-Mega (Sludge Bomb OHKO) and Alakazam-Mega (Shadow Ball) at the right moment. Gholdengo as 4th is the defensive anchor: resists Fairy/Psychic, immune to Fighting (Scrafty), Good as Gold blocks Taunt/TWave/WoW, and Make It Rain hits Floette SE. Against expected Scrafty+Floette lead, Protect Excadrill to block Fake Out while Tyranitar Rock Slides; turn 2 Excadrill Iron Heads Floette before it moves.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 lead: Tyranitar+Excadrill (sand core), back Gengar+Gholdengo. Sand Stream on entry means Excadrill Sand Rush active T1 (280 Spe). Key damage notes: Excadrill Iron Head 2x on Floette, Rock Slide 4x on Talonflame, High Horsepower 2x on Garchomp. Gengar-Mega 200 Spe outspeeds all except Alakazam-Mega (187-222). Sludge Bomb OHKOs Floette-Mega (53-109%), Shadow Ball OHKOs Alakazam-Mega (64-148%). Gholdengo resists Fairy/Psychic, immune Fighting, Good as Gold blocks status. Opponent likely leads Scrafty+Floette (rematch pattern); counter-lead threat is Talonflame+Garchomp (Gale Wings BB + Life Orb EQ). Plan: Protect Excadrill T1 vs Fake Out, Tyranitar Rock Slides; bring Gengar in to trap and KO Floette-Mega with Shadow Tag + Sludge Bomb.

decisions.rationale: Pivot Alakazam out of Tyranitar’s guaranteed Crunch KO while Protect denies Excadrill’s guaranteed Iron Head KO on Floette; Garchomp creates the strongest immediate counterpressure into both opposing actives next turn.

Excadrill Iron Head on Floette (2x SE, 86-169%, potential OHKO) removes the primary threat to Tyranitar. Tyranitar Crunch on Alakazam (2x SE, 89-195%, potential OHKO) removes the speed/Mega threat. Tyranitar survives any single Floette hit (max 70.5% from Light of Ruin), and Alakazam cannot meaningfully damage Tyranitar (Psychic immune, Shadow Ball NVE). Double-targeting both foes at 280 Speed with Excadrill guarantees damage before either opponent moves unless Alakazam-Mega Traces Sand Rush (50% chance). Even then, Excadrill's Iron Head still resolves on Floette, and Tyranitar's Crunch still hits Alakazam-Mega for massive damage.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 T1: Led Tyranitar+Excadrill vs Alakazam+Floette (not predicted Scrafty lead). Excadrill Iron Head 86-169% on Floette (possible OHKO). Tyranitar Crunch 89-195% on Alakazam (possible OHKO). Floette Moonblast 33-49% on Tyranitar, Light of Ruin 49-70% (survives both). Alakazam-Mega Trace risk: 50% chance to copy Sand Rush (187-222×2=374-444, outspeeds Excadrill 280) vs Sand Stream. Plan T2: if both foes survive, finish with Excadrill speed; bring Gengar-Mega mid-game for Shadow Tag trapping. Gholdengo in back for Fairy/Psychic resist + Good as Gold status immunity. Watch for back Pokémon: Garchomp (EQ+Rough Skin), Talonflame (Gale Wings BB), Scrafty (Fake Out+Intimidate), Milotic (Competitive+Scald).

decisions.rationale: Preserve both Garchomp and Floette from their immediate guaranteed KO threats; Talonflame can absorb the likely Iron Head while Garchomp safely blocks Ice Punch or other pressure.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Tyranitar is Careful with Smooth Rock and Sand Stream; revealed moves are Rock Slide, Crunch, Ice Punch, Protect. Opponent Excadrill is Adamant with Focus Sash and Sand Rush; revealed moves are Iron Head, Rock Slide, High Horsepower, Protect. Maintain Mega Alakazam as the preferred answer to potential Mega Gengar; preserve Mega Floette for endgames after Steel/Ghost pressure is controlled.

decisions.rationale: Excadrill Iron Head on Floette (~87% KO chance) removes the Fairy threat before Tyranitar acts; Tyranitar Ice Punch on Garchomp (4x SE, 56-101% on 64% HP) likely KOs or cripples it. Garchomp EQ is discouraged (39-91% friendly fire on Floette ally). If Floette falls, Tyranitar survives any single Garchomp hit (Stomping Tantrum ≤80% vs 88% HP) to deliver Ice Punch. Even worst-case (Floette survives, both focus Tyranitar), Excadrill survives via Focus Sash to clean up next turn.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 T2: Excadrill Iron Head 86-169% on Floette (94% HP, ~87% KO). Tyranitar Ice Punch 56-101% on Garchomp (64% HP, possible KO). Garchomp EQ does 39-91% to own Floette ally (strong deterrent). Garchomp Stomping Tantrum 57-80% on Tyranitar (survives at 88%). Floette Moonblast 33-49% / Light of Ruin 49-70% on Tyranitar. Combined Garchomp+Floette damage can KO Tyranitar before it acts if both target it (~13% scenario when Floette survives Iron Head). Alakazam in back with Alakazite (Mega Trace: 50% Sand Rush copy → 374-444 speed outspeeding Excadrill 280). Plan: if both foes KO'd, bring Gengar-Mega for Shadow Tag trapping; Gholdengo for Fairy/Psychic resist. Watch for back Pokémon: Talonflame (Gale Wings BB), Scrafty (Fake Out+Intimidate), Milotic (Competitive+Scald).

decisions.rationale: Earthquake maximizes simultaneous damage into both foes while Talonflame pressures Excadrill through Focus Sash and can remove it before Garchomp acts if Rock Slide does not stop Talonflame.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Tyranitar is Careful with Smooth Rock, Sand Stream, Rock Slide, Crunch, Ice Punch, and Protect. Opponent Excadrill is Adamant with Focus Sash, Sand Rush, Iron Head, Rock Slide, High Horsepower, and Protect. Preserve Mega Alakazam as the preferred answer to potential Mega Gengar; reserve Mega Floette for endgames after Steel/Ghost pressure is controlled.

decisions.rationale: Bring in both remaining Pokémon; Alakazam and Floette together retain immediate pressure on Tyranitar while keeping Mega Alakazam available for a potential Mega Gengar endgame.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s revealed Tyranitar is Careful Smooth Rock Sand Stream with Rock Slide, Crunch, Ice Punch, Protect. Revealed Excadrill is Adamant Focus Sash Sand Rush with Iron Head, Rock Slide, High Horsepower, Protect. Preserve Mega Alakazam as the preferred answer to potential Mega Gengar; reserve Mega Floette for endgames after Steel/Ghost pressure is controlled.

decisions.rationale: Excadrill Rock Slide (280 Spe, guaranteed first since Gale Wings is inactive at 57% HP) guaranteed KOs Talonflame (4x SE, 78-149% vs 57%) and chips Garchomp 7-12% with 30% flinch. Tyranitar Ice Punch hits Garchomp for 4x SE (56-101%); with Rock Slide chip Garchomp drops to ~52-57%, making KO near-certain. Even if Garchomp EQs first (54-80% to Tyranitar who survives at 8-34%, Excadrill saved by Focus Sash), Ice Punch still KOs afterward. If Garchomp Protects (reduced rate), Rock Slide still removes Talonflame. Best expected value: likely double KO, forcing Alakazam+Floette in against our board advantage.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 T3: Gale Wings confirmed INACTIVE when Talonflame <100% HP — Excadrill 280 outspeeds all foe mons when no priority. Excadrill Rock Slide guaranteed KO on Talonflame at 57% (4x SE, 78-149%). Tyranitar Ice Punch 56-101% on Garchomp (4x SE), near-guaranteed KO with any Rock Slide chip. Garchomp EQ 54-80% on Tyranitar (survives from 88%), 110-158% on Excadrill (Focus Sash saves). If both foes KO'd, expect Alakazam-Mega (Trace, 187-222 Spe) + Floette-Eternal in back. Watch: Alakazam-Mega Trace has 50% chance to copy Sand Rush → 374-444 Spe outspeeding Excadrill 280. Plan: bring Gengar-Mega (Shadow Tag) or Gholdengo (Steel/Ghost resists Psychic/Fairy) as appropriate. Floette-Eternal at 94% survived Excadrill Iron Head (86-169%, ~87% KO chance) T2 — likely took ~6% from spread/LO chip. Garchomp Protect used T2 (reduced success rate T3+).

selection: Light of Ruin -> foe 1 (Tyranitar) + Mega Evolve
decisions.rationale: Protect Alakazam from Tyranitar’s guaranteed Crunch KO while Mega Floette uses its strongest Fairy attack to maximize the chance of immediately removing Tyranitar before Excadrill can attack.
decisions.notebook: Opponent revealed Careful Smooth Rock Sand Stream Tyranitar with Rock Slide, Crunch, Ice Punch, Protect; and Adamant Focus Sash Sand Rush Excadrill with Iron Head, Rock Slide, High Horsepower, Protect. Sand Rush Excadrill is an extreme speed threat in sand and Focus Sash must be accounted for. Potential unrevealed options include Mega Gengar, Gholdengo, Grimmsnarl, and Rotom.

decisions.rationale: Double SE target: Tyranitar Crunch on Alakazam (88.9-195.4%, possible OHKO) and Excadrill Iron Head on Floette (86.2-169.1%, possible KO from 94%). Tyranitar survives any single Floette hit even at 76% (Light of Ruin max 70.5%). Alakazam's damage on both my mons is weak (Psychic immune on TTar, NVE on Excadrill; Shadow Ball NVE on both). Even if Alakazam Megas and Traces Sand Rush (50%), it can't KO Excadrill (max 42%). If Floette Protects, Tyranitar stays at 76% and we adapt next turn with bench options. This is the highest-EV play: two potential KOs with minimal risk.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 T4: Aggressive double SE target (Crunch→Alakazam 89-195%, Iron Head→Floette 86-169%). TTar survives any single Floette hit from 76%. Alakazam-Mega Trace 50% Sand Rush → 374-444 Spe outspeeds Excadrill 280 but can't KO it (Shadow Ball max 42%, Psychic NVE). Sand 5 turns left. Bench: Gengar-Mega (Shadow Tag, weak to Psychic/Ghost) and Gholdengo (Steel/Ghost, resists Fairy/Ghost, Good as Gold blocks status) for late-game. If Floette survives at low HP, finish next turn. If TTar drops below ~30%, switch to Gholdengo to tank Floette's Fairy moves. Plan for G2: opponent brought Alakazam+Garchomp+Talonflame+Floette; Scrafty+Milotic in back. Expect similar lead; consider Gholdengo lead if opponent adapts.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Reduced-success Protect is the only available action that can prevent the otherwise immediate guaranteed Crunch knockout and preserves the only plausible path through opponent misses or errors.
decisions.notebook: Tyranitar is Careful with Smooth Rock, Sand Stream, Rock Slide, Crunch, Ice Punch, and Protect. Excadrill is Adamant Focus Sash Sand Rush with Iron Head, Rock Slide, High Horsepower, and Protect; it outspeeds Alakazam in sand. Preserve anti-sand counterplay and account for Excadrill's Focus Sash in future games.

decisions.rationale: Opponent has only Alakazam remaining (3/4 fainted). Crunch (88.9-195.4%) + Iron Head (59.3-130%) = 148.2% minimum combined damage, guaranteeing the KO regardless of Alakazam's hidden spread. Iron Head chosen over High Horsepower for 100% accuracy (vs 95%) and flinch chance since Excadrill (280 Spe) outspeeds base Alakazam. Even if Alakazam Mega Evolves and Traces Sand Rush (50%), it can't KO either Pokémon (Shadow Ball max 42% on Excadrill, Psychic NVE). If Alakazam Protects (reduced rate after T4), it only delays the inevitable 1v4. No risk; go for the kill.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent brought Alakazam+Garchomp+Talonflame+Floette-Mega; Scrafty+Milotic in back. Garchomp KO'd T3 (Ice Punch), Talonflame KO'd T3 (Rock Slide), Floette-Mega KO'd T4 (Iron Head SE). Alakazam is last Pokémon standing. Alakazam-Mega Trace 50% Sand Rush → 374-444 Spe outspeeds Excadrill 280 but cannot KO it (Shadow Ball max 42%, Psychic NVE). Excadrill Focus Sash intact. Bench: Gengar-Mega (Shadow Tag) and Gholdengo (Good as Gold) unused. Plan for G2: expect similar lead; consider Gholdengo lead if opponent adapts to sand. Watch for Scrafty Intimidate and Milotic Competitive if opponent brings them G2.

reflections.summary: Lost to Tyranitar–Excadrill sand pressure: Sand Rush gave Excadrill the speed advantage, and the Rock Slide flinch plus follow-up Ice Punch removed Garchomp and Talonflame before they could establish offense. The four brought were not well suited to this lead because they lacked a reliable immediate answer to the sand core; Mega Floette was especially vulnerable to Excadrill’s Iron Head. Mega Alakazam would have been the more suitable evolution for speed control versus sand.
reflections.adjustment: Next game, prioritize Mega Alakazam and lead or preserve it with a partner that pressures Tyranitar/Excadrill immediately; do not rely on Talonflame or Garchomp surviving Rock Slide plus Ice Punch to set up Tailwind or attack.
reflections.notebook: Opponent led Tyranitar–Excadrill in game 1, indicating a willingness to open with immediate sand-speed pressure. Tyranitar is Careful Smooth Rock Sand Stream with Rock Slide, Crunch, Ice Punch, and Protect. Excadrill is Adamant Focus Sash Sand Rush with Iron Head, Rock Slide, High Horsepower, and Protect; it outspeeds non-Mega Alakazam in sand. Plan for Focus Sash and prioritize Mega Alakazam or other immediate anti-sand speed control; avoid exposing Talonflame and Garchomp together to Rock Slide/Ice Punch pressure.

reflections.summary: Sand core of Tyranitar + Excadrill swept through the opponent's entire team in 5 turns. Excadrill under Sand Rush outsped everything, Iron Head KO'd Floette-Mega and Alakazam, while Rock Slide flinched Garchomp T3 enabling the clean double KO. Opponent's Protect-heavy play couldn't generate enough pressure to break the sand speed advantage.
reflections.adjustment: Opponent will likely adapt by bringing Scrafty (Intimidate/Fake Out) or Milotic (Competitive/Icy Wind) to disrupt sand. Consider leading Gholdengo alongside Tyranitar if you expect Scrafty Fake Out, since Good as Gold blocks Snarl and Make It Rain pressures Milotic. Gengar-Mega was unused—only bring if Shadow Tag trapping is needed for a specific lead.
reflections.notebook: Opponent roster: Alakazam (Alakazite, Timid, Magic Guard→Trace when Mega), Garchomp (Life Orb, Jolly, Rough Skin), Talonflame (Focus Sash, Jolly, Gale Wings), Floette-Mega (Floettite, Timid, Fairy Aura), Scrafty (Roseli Berry, Careful, Intimidate), Milotic (Leftovers, Bold, Competitive). G1 brought: Alakazam+Garchomp+Talonflame+Floette; benched Scrafty+Milotic. Opponent plays Protect-heavy, tends to protect predicted targets rather than switch. Floette-Mega confirmed Fairy Aura. Alakazam never Mega Evolved G1 (KO'd before it could). Sand core (Tyranitar+Excadrill) dominated; Gengar-Mega and Gholdengo unused. G2 plan: expect opponent to adapt with Scrafty Intimidate/Fake Out or Milotic Competitive/Icy Wind to slow sand. If Scrafty brought, lead Gholdengo to absorb Snarl and threaten Make It Rain. Alakazam-Mega Trace under sand copies Sand Rush (374+ Spe) but cannot KO Excadrill (Shadow Ball max 42%, Psychic NVE). Excadrill Focus Sash still intact.
